Howbeit
how-BEE-it
adverb
A compound of “how,” “be,” and “it” — literally “how (ever) it be” — an Old-English-rooted conjunction meaning “nevertheless,” “however,” or “yet notwithstanding.”

Biblical Definition

Howbeit is the KJV’s great word of turning — “nevertheless, however, be it as it may” — the hinge on which a sentence pivots from one truth to a weightier one. It can mark the blindness of unbelief: “Howbeit we know this man whence he is: but when Christ cometh, no man knoweth whence he is” (Joh 7:27) — the “howbeit” introducing the false certainty that shut Jerusalem’s eyes to her own Messiah. It can guard the weak conscience: “Howbeit there is not in every man that knowledge” (1Co 8:7), Paul turning from the freedom of the strong to the tenderness owed the weak. It can name the one weapon for a stubborn evil: “Howbeit this kind goeth not out but by prayer and fasting” (Mat 17:21). And it can lay bare the searching hand of God: “Howbeit in the business of the ambassadors… God left him, to try him, that he might know all that was in his heart” (2Ch 32:31) — Hezekiah’s pride exposed by the very silence of God. In each place the little word does heavy work: it refuses to let the first clause stand alone, and bends the reader toward the deeper or the truer thing. The Scripture reasons; it qualifies; it turns. Let the reader learn to feel the weight of every “howbeit,” for the whole difference between error and truth, presumption and grace, often hangs upon it.

Webster 1828 Definition

“Nevertheless, however” — the KJV’s hinge-word that turns a sentence from one truth toward a weightier one.

expand to see more

HOWBEIT, nevertheless; however; be it as it may; yet notwithstanding.

A compound of “how,” “be,” and “it” — “how(ever) it be.”

It introduces the false certainty of unbelief (Joh 7:27).

It turns the strong toward the weak conscience (1Co 8:7).

It names the one cure for a stubborn evil: prayer and fasting (Mat 17:21).

Key Scripture

Joh 7:27 — "Howbeit we know this man whence he is: but when Christ cometh, no man knoweth whence he is."

1Co 8:7 — "Howbeit there is not in every man that knowledge: for some with conscience of the idol unto this hour eat it as a thing offered unto an idol; and their conscience being weak is defiled."

Mat 17:21 — "Howbeit this kind goeth not out but by prayer and fasting."

2Ch 32:31 — "Howbeit in the business of the ambassadors of the princes of Babylon, who sent unto him to enquire of the wonder that was done in the land, God left him, to try him, that he might know all that was in his heart."

Modern Corruption

Not a contested doctrine but a lost conjunction; recovering it restores the sinews of Scripture’s reasoning — the turns on which truth hangs.

expand to see more

The loss the word marks is the loss of careful reading. Scripture argues; it qualifies; it turns on words like “howbeit,” “nevertheless,” “but God.” An age that reads in fragments, hunting a verse to feel and skipping the hinge that governs it, misses the very logic of revelation. Jerusalem’s fatal “howbeit we know this man” (Joh 7:27) shows how a confident clause, left unturned, can shut the eyes against Christ. The hinges are where the reasoning lives.

This entry faces no significant postmodern redefinition. The principle to recover is reverent, connected reading — feeling the weight of every turn the Spirit gives His argument. “Howbeit” refuses to let a half-truth stand; it bends us toward the weaker brother, the harder cure, the searching of God. To honor the conjunctions of Scripture is to honor its Author’s reasoning, and to read as men who would be taught, not merely stirred (2Ti 2:15).

Greek & Hebrew Roots

“How it be” — a homely English compound that became the KJV’s strong word for “nevertheless,” the hinge of its reasoning.

expand to see more

Howbeit — “how,” “be,” “it”: literally “how(ever) it be.”

It means nevertheless, however, yet notwithstanding.

It marks the false certainty that hid Christ from Jerusalem (Joh 7:27).

It turns the strong to spare the weak conscience (1Co 8:7).

It names the cure for stubborn evil: prayer and fasting (Mat 17:21).

Usage

"The whole difference between error and truth may hang on a howbeit."

"Scripture reasons and turns; learn to feel the weight of the hinge."

"Howbeit refuses to let the first clause stand alone."
